newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo to buy 18.3 pct Lonrho.
newsitem.headline: Anglo to buy 18.3 pct Lonrho.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday that it would acquire a further 18.3 percent of Lonrho Plc at 180 pence per share.

"Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd today received notice from Laerstate BV, a company owned by Mr Dieter Bock, of the exercise of Laerstate's right to sell its 18.3 percent outstanding shareholdings in Lonrho Plc to Anglo American at the exercise price of 180p per share," Anglo said in a statement.
"Following the completion of this transaction, Anglo American and companies associated with it will own 25.9 percent of the outstanding share capital of Lonrho," it added.
In addition, Southern Life Association Ltd -- in which Anglo holds a significant stake -- has a 2.2 percent interest in Lonrho, of which 0.5 percent is held for clients.
Anglo said it would fund the transaction by drawing down on its offshore facilities and would therefore not be acquiring foreign currency for this transaction in the short-term.
Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said that the group did not intend to make an offer for Lonrho's outstanding shares.
"Anglo American's shareholding in Lonrho represents a long-term investment and it does not intend to make a general offer for the outstanding shares of Lonrho," he said.
He added that Anglo supported Lonrho's intention to unbundle its mining and non-mining businesses.
"Over the long term Anglo American looks forward to supporting and contributing to Lonrho's mining business," he said.
Lonrho holds more than 30 percent of Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd and Ogilvie Thompson said he hoped this latest transaction would further enhance Anglo's "good relationship" with Ashanti.
This, he said, Anglo hoped to do "by mutual exchange of technology and expertise and, perhaps in the future, partnerships in new ventures in Africa.
Anglo said that Ogilvie Thompson and a delegation of senior executives recently held talks in Ghana with the country's president Jerry Rawlings and senior members of government.
